author: Hugh Jass
content:
Easy satire made by "smart" person for other "smart" people like him, the millenial version of terrible political comics made by 80 year olds. An easy position to take with no downsides when everything is black and white and has no gradients and anything that might counter this position simply stops existing when I feel like it stops existing. The kind of person whose beliefs and worldview break down the moment he faces reality outside of his walled garden, if he ever does. A list of words that are simply meant to evoke a primal emotion rather than explain an argument. Worst of all, horribly unfunny and meandering by the structure alone.
You may think you're a unique little snowflake, but you're a true dime a million, stuck in a little box and incapable of serious discussion or reflection, only being able to parrot in different terms what others have invented before you. Whether or not this is an intrinsic failure on your part or the fault of those who've taught you, nobody knows, but either way you'll continue to make these lame unthoughtful posts for presumably the rest of your life, never being capable of anything truly unique and always walking in others shadows. No smug counter from anyone will change this for you.

author: Michael Peters
content: The message of this (we need gun control) doesn't bother me but the arrogance does. If you come to a certain conclusion about a complex issue like gun control and also believe that everyone who didn't has all the qualities implied in the checklist, it doesn't reflect well on you. You must believe that it is impossible for you to have failed to consider something that those who disagree with you have. Considering yourself more intelligent than every member of a very large and diverse group of people (those who are against whatever particular gun control you support) seems very self-centered to me.

author: Ringo
content:
Nice list Josh! I came here after showing my daughter your incredibly insight-improving "If the Moon were only one pixel". Good to see you provide other interesting insights too.

Of course, where I am (Netherlands) this form is quite unneeded because no member of the public can buy an assault weapon, ever. These are reserved for the military and special police forces.
Which I guess to the poster above makes the Netherlands "intrinsically racist, fascist, sexist, homophobic, transphobic, and authoritarian". I would have thought the opposite. Maybe the poster above should visit gay pride in Amsterdam (august 1st to 6th). Without a gun, of course.
